core.title: Escape every bare value interpolated into a markup fragment
core.given: Server-side code builds a markup fragment as an interpolated string (a markup-bearing string, its text containing an opening tag), and the client inserts it into the page as markup with no auto-escaping anywhere in the path
core.when: a value is interpolated into that markup
core.then: Never interpolate a bare value (a variable or property reference) directly into the markup; route the value through an escaping helper at the interpolation site.
prefer: Escape at the interpolation site: the value passes through the escaping helper inside the markup expression — escaped at the boundary.
Escape at the RENDER site, where the destination is known, so it is escaped exactly once.
Nest fragments via calls whose inner fragments escape their own data.
avoid: A bare value dropped straight into the markup — raw data into the rendered fragment.
Escaping at storage/fetch: double-escaped when it reaches a non-markup sink.
An interpolation that is a call which neither escapes nor nests: it passes the check, but is still a violation; review catches it.
Carrying over the bare-interpolation habit from a stack whose markup interpolation is auto-escaped, assuming the escaping still happens invisibly underneath.
unless: The string contains no markup (no opening tag; not markup — never scanned).
The interpolation is a call, treated as escaping or composition (check scope; non-escaping calls remain a review concern).
Test files, identified positively by the profile's test-file name patterns.
core.why: In a stack whose component markup auto-escapes interpolated values, escaping is implicit; in a string-interpolation fragment pipeline it is explicit. Carrying over bare interpolation without the invisible escaping yields stored XSS in code that looks like what the team wrote before.
evidence: This rule's markup-escape check reports zero bare-value interpolation findings in markup-bearing strings of non-test source files.
No interpolation in a markup-bearing string is a bare variable or property reference; operator and literal expressions are outside this rule's scope.
Review checks call interpolations that neither escape nor nest, since the check passes them.
Values are escaped at the render site, not at storage/fetch (no double-escaping in non-markup sinks).
verification: A static check over non-test production source flags every interpolation into a markup-bearing string whose expression is only a bare value (a variable or property reference). A string counts as markup-bearing when its text contains an opening tag — the signal it is markup rather than a log line, query string or URL; strings without an opening tag are never scanned. This opening-tag criterion and the no-auto-escaping condition are part of the rule, not profile data.
The check scans every markup-bearing string in non-test source in scope, not only changed ones; the change fact is an activation hint for the coder, not the check's scope.

Interpolations that are calls are deliberately out of the check's scope (they may be escape helpers or fragment composition, and flagging them would bury the rule in false positives on legitimate composition). A call that neither escapes nor nests passes the check and must be caught by review — the narrowing is the price of a precise signal a team will not switch off.
Test files are excluded from the check; the exclusion is the rule's policy, and the profile's test-file name patterns identify test files positively, without assigning them to a specific test role.
Disposition strict, severity 1 — this is the security rule of the hypermedia fragment rules.

this rule's markup-escape check: bare value interpolation in a markup-bearing string

fires: A boundary or presentation handler returns a markup fragment that the page inserts as markup, with a value interpolated directly between or inside its tags.

doesNotFire: A string with no markup in it (a log line, a query string, a URL) — never scanned.
An interpolation that is a call, e.g. an escape helper or a fragment-composition call (check-wise; a non-escaping call is still a review concern).

neutralityNotes: The obligation itself (no bare value into markup; escape at the interpolation/render site) is fully neutral, and the opening-tag markup-bearing criterion and the no-auto-escaping condition are part of the rule text, not profile data. Per the audit fixes: idiom.markup_kinds carries artifact-kind data only (server-rendered HTML fragment); the interpolated-string construct is bound through the vocabulary v3 map entry idiom.markup#markup_interpolation (idiom.markup's documented interpolation meaning — no new key needed, no proposal made); and the test-file exclusion is expressed with positive test-file name patterns under suffix.test (**/*.test.*, **/*.spec.*, exactly the Bun test-file scope, described generally with no unit/acceptance role assignment), while the exclusion policy itself stays in core:verification. What could not be made neutral and stays in the Bun realization: the template-literal/backtick interpolation syntax and its brace-depth-aware extraction mechanics, the concrete examples (`${escapeHtml(order.title)}`, `${format(bio)}`), the JSX comparison, the htmx/hx-swap/innerHTML insertion details, this rule's detector/finding ids (htmx_hypermedia_detector, bare_interpolation), and the negated-exclusion-glob spelling. The check's deliberate narrowness (calls out of scope, non-escaping calls left to review) and the strict/severity-1 enforcement are kept in core:verification, so instantiation with the Bun profile plus these bunOnly items imposes exactly the bun.json obligation — no exceptions dropped, none added.
